title: Exact Sequential Lifting over Cyclic Groups: Circular Envelopes of the Value Function
content: Exact sequential lifting for a bounded modular knapsack reads each coefficient from the value function on the cyclic group Zq. The function is stored as a circular envelope, a list of maximal runs of one forward symbol, using two symbols on edges that meet minus infinity. The envelope determines the function. A zero-one update multiplies the number of runs by at most six. The ratio three is attained, and the proof of the factor six does not reach three, so a universal constant for that bound lies between 3 and 6. For the weights 2i−1, the prescribed profits 3i−1 give length 2k when q=2k and length 2k+1 when q>2k. On a complete sequence with equal efficiency, every prefix has length at most three, and the arithmetic is then linear in the number of variables. Shifting the first profit by a sufficiently small nonzero amount returns the length to 2k or 2k+1. For finite bounds, the envelope algorithm and the residue-table recurrence return the same coefficients.
